shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Levels and per-level size are bought from a fixed 146,000-cell budget. Per-colony climate bands make high levels genuinely alpine, with snow, altitude weather and windier peaks. Coast, river and lake tiles supported; Dubs Mint Minimap and Map Preview both patched.
body:
# As above, So below II (V2)

> V1 is DELETED. ~66 files, ~17,900 LOC. No em-dashes anywhere in shipped text; keep it that way.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities in order: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

## Status
Visuality, QOL, altitude/weather and settings passes are all VERIFIED IN PLAY. Top open item is generation cost (§9).

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount * Slot)`. Bands stack along +z from the deepest basement, with a permanently-fogged gutter between them. `Slot = ceil((bandHeight+2)/64)*64`; **64-alignment is load-bearing** (terrain shaders sample by world position, so a non-multiple offset makes the ground "randomise" between a level and its see-below view). Per-level sizes 126 / 190 / 254.

**The one insight.** `Region.Neighbors` is *topological, not spatial*. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms, temperature or vacuum, and `Reachability.CanReach` works unpatched. But reachability is not a path: 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

**Hard 1.6 constraints.** The path grid is an IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell, so total stacked cells is the runtime metric. No `PathFinder.FindPath`. `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

**⚠ The stack is 2x to 7x anisotropic.** Anything vanilla normalises by BOTH map dimensions is distorted, and that bug class cannot appear on an ordinary square map. First suspect for any "smeared or stretched" symptom.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE, six shapes
The surface band is a horizontal SLICE of a tall map, so anything vanilla anchors to the map's extent lands in the wrong band.

| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor, a point picked as a fraction of `Size.z` | river and lake centre; random/edge cell (§15a) | remap the point |
| Field, a gradient centred on the map centre | coastline (§6e) | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| Noise space, a slice is not a short map | Map Preview (§6d) | generate at full height, then crop |
| Distance-to-extent, a margin measured off `Size` | `CloseToEdge`, no-build edge (§15b, §15d) | re-base onto the cell's own band rect |
| Aspect ratio, normalised by BOTH dims | water surface (§6b-LAKE) | none, cosmetic, accepted |
| **Map-wide scalar**, one per-tick value for the whole map | snow melt (§7), temperature readout (§16) | rewrite it per cell at the consumer |

Classify a new bug into one of these six, but PROVE it. Map-wide scalar is the nastiest: the value is correct, just not per-band, so nothing looks wrong in the code. Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all use `FalloffAtAngle`).

# 2. LEVEL PLAN, budget 146,000 cells, FIXED
`4 x 190 = 145,920` sets the figure. `5 x 190` and `3 x 254` are refused. `ABMapSizeLimit` owns it.
Per-level size is SQUARE (`Size.x == bandHeight`), which is why `GenStep_Scatterer.CountFromPer10kCells` (it squares `Size.x`, not `map.Area`) already yields a per-BAND count. Only `GenStep_AnimaTrees` and `GenStep_TerrainPatches` read `map.Area`.

**⚠ The level chooser is also the lab.** `0 above / 0 below` generates an ORDINARY single-level map, which is the vanilla control for "is this even our bug". Band count sets `Size.z`, so the chooser is a calibrated aspect dial: 1 band = 1.00, 2 = 2.02, 4 = 4.04.
**⚠ STILL UNVERIFIED: does `0 up / 0 down` actually reach generation?** Run #174 was launched to be that control and produced a 190x768 four-band map anyway. Pre-flight check: the strip must read 1 level and 36,100 cells.

**⚠ The chooser UI: own the widget, do not patch the data.** `Dialog_AdvancedGameConfig.MapSizes` is `static readonly` and the reflection swap SILENTLY FAILED in play; the postfix also re-snapped `GameInitData.mapSize` every frame, undoing every click. Now our own radio buttons write `mapSize` directly. Window grown via an `InitialSize` postfix, because vanilla lays its columns from the top and never consults the height.

# 3. CROSS-BAND MOVEMENT
Segmented at ONE interception: `StartPath` prefix, tick sweep, `Carry` re-issues `StartPath`. `ABWormhole.TryGetTransit` BFSes the band graph; hops must strictly decrease or pawns ping-pong. **Multi-hop routing is STILL UNTESTED IN PLAY** (needs a stair tower).

# 4. GROUP ORDERING
Three wrong layers before the right one. Correct answer: `RecomputeDestinations` spreads the selection along the drag line, which between bands runs through the GUTTER. The odd/even signature ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 do not") is the proof, because only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5. Fix is to normalise `start`/`end` into the commanded pawns' band. Verified.

# 5. ⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE: `ABBands.TryResolveVisibleBelow`
Descends while each level is see-through, stops at the first opaque floor or the bottom band, returns the accumulated drop. NINE systems share it. **Seven separate appearances of the single `- Slot` bug**; grep every `- Slot` before trusting new code.
Sun-shadow subtlety: its mask is neighbour-based, so mask and descent are answered together by `TryResolveDropAround`, taking the smallest drop among the nine cells.
Still single-band: the realtime-things pass in `ABBelowDynamicDraw` (motes, fire).

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION (verified)
Four rejected attempts are on record: force-linked wall masks, high-queue cover, wall-sprite suppression, and theorising twice about "flat" mountains before running the below-layer report.
Despeckle (walls dissolve only at 7+ open neighbours; at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge), one central fog hole, five-terrain plateau palette, cliff faces, alpine pass.
**⚠ The mass tapers with altitude, so +3 may contain NO LAND AT ALL.** This was mistaken for "snow is broken at +3" in run #178. Check for ground before diagnosing anything about the top level.
Ore glyph bug: ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`, so a "can't happen" fallback drew the whole atlas sheet per cell.

# 6b. ⚠ WATER: 1.6 water is a TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE effect
`SectionLayer_Watergen` (vanilla, `internal`, cannot be subclassed) is `SectionLayer_Terrain` plus `waterDepthMaterial`, drawn to the WaterDepth SUBCAMERA's layer. The visible `Map/TerrainWater` material samples that texture at its own SCREEN position. Printing the water material where the depth pass never wrote yields nothing at all.
- Water missing from upper levels, FIXED: `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` mirrors the internal Watergen and overrides `DrawLayer` to target `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`.
- Rivers not generating, FIXED: remap `GetRiverCenter` (not `Init`, which consumes it immediately) preserving the roll. `GetLakeCenter` needs the same patch or it undoes the first.
- The flow path is band-correct and PROVEN IRRELEVANT to the streaking (see below).

# 6b-LAKE. CLOSED: surface streaking accepted as vanilla appearance
PROVEN in run #173: a tile with water but no water mutators (`riverGraph 0`, `riverFlowMap NULL`, `riverFlowTexture null`, `water=580`, `baseRiver=0`) still streaked. No flow data exists in the process, so flow cannot be the cause. **The ghost-river theory is dead; do not revive it.** Root cause never established, and the user's call was to stop. Found en route: vanilla's flow builder ends `zero /= (float)num3` with no zero guard, so a river cell outside every sample radius writes NaN into a bilinear-filtered texture.

# 6c, 6d, 6e. COMPAT AND COASTS (all verified)
**Dubs Mint Minimap:** ONE RECT, not seven patches, because their six draw passes all take the same `radarRect` and are linear in position. `DrawTextureFitted` preserves the TEXTURE's aspect, so use `ScaleMode.StretchToFill`. Reflection only, no foreign type in any patch-class signature.
**Map Preview:** it never calls `MapGenerator.GenerateMap`, and a slice of position-based noise is a different map, not a slightly wrong one. Fix is to generate at full stacked height and crop via `TexCoords`. `MaxMapSize.z` MUST rise (default 500, a stack reaches 896). Read their own `ModCompat_BetterMapSizes` first; half the work is two public static field assignments.
**Coasts:** CENTRED wrong, not scaled wrong. `map.Size.z` appears in `FalloffAtAngle` exactly once, in the final centring translate. Fix is `z' = (z % Slot) + (map.Size.z - bandHeight) / 2`, with NO SCALING (scaling would skew every non-axis-aligned coast and make displacement noise anisotropic). Nine coastal mutators, none override `GetNoiseValue`.

# 7. PER-LEVEL CHARACTER
Ore `x(1 + 0.45*(depth-1))`, cave openness `x(1 + 0.35*(depth-1))`, both applied AFTER the settings clamp.

**⚠ The snow line never worked, and the comment saying it did not need to was wrong.** Generation-time seeding was deleted on the grounds that "vanilla melts snow using each cell's own temperature". False. `SteadyEnvironmentEffectsTick` computes `outdoorMeltAmount = MeltAmountAt(map.mapTemperature.OutdoorTemp)` once per tick for the whole map and never calls `TryGetTemperatureForCell`. The line was dead for months behind a confident, wrong sentence.

**Climate defaults** (now per colony, §17): +1 = -7, +2 = -16, +3 = -35, basement flat -6, wind x1.15 / x1.30 / x1.50. +2 is the seasonal snow line, +3 a permanent cap that a desert or a heat wave can still thaw. **No ceiling clamp by design**, because melt must stay a consequence of real temperature or an extreme biome could never overcome it.

# 8. CAMERA
`ABCameraBounds.For(level)` keyed by LEVEL, not band index. `maxZoom` left DERIVED (an absolute mis-scales a 190 band). `panMargin` 63.5 now applies to EVERY level; there was never a per-level reason for the old split, and the view clip guarantees overhang shows curtain, never the neighbouring level. `Dialog_ABCameraCalibration` opens with the clamp UNLOCKED, because a calibration tool must suspend the limit it calibrates.

# 9. ⚠ GENERATION COST (top open item)
| Run | Tile | Carve | band1 | band2 | band3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #173 | bog | 2.3 s | | | |
| #174 | mountainous | 17.1 s | 3.6 | 8.5 | 4.8 |
| #175 | mountainous | 17.4 s | 10.9 | 3.3 | 2.7 |
| #176 | mountainous | 18.5 s | 10.7 | 4.4 | 2.8 |

**Biome content drives cost, not cell count:** 7.4x spread at identical size and band count.  Any carve timing MUST record the tile or it is meaningless.
**⚠ FALSIFIED: "band 1 is consistently ~3x bands 2-3."** #174 and #175 are the same config with reversed distributions. Per-band cost is a property of where that tile's noise put rock. **The doomed-band skip must scope all non-surface bands uniformly and cannot be tuned per band.**
`Sky clear` is ~97% of the carve and `0 rocks spawned`, so everything destroyed is content generated into doomed bands and immediately deleted. `SeedAltitudeSnow` costs 17.8 ms, free.
Precedent for the fix: `Patch_WildPlantSpawner_ABSkipDoomedBands` took 16.9 s to 4.2 s.
**Hard constraint:** per-cell gensteps scope safely, `map.Area`-count scatterers do not (the scatterer family counts off `Size.x^2`, so it is safe). Do not blanket-skip the water or coast mutators; §6b, §6e and §6d depend on them running correctly anchored.

# 10, 11. PERF AND LINKS
59.6 fps at 96 pawns, mod approximately 2% of frame. All rendering is bake-time section-mesh geometry. Elevator SHIPPED but untested; full-mesh 2x2, O(n^2) in band count.

# 12. DIAGNOSTICS
Band info, below layer and pawn reports, water report, transit health, stuck probe, lighting/shader/biome reports, bisect toggles, ABGenProfile, camera calibration.
**⚠ Bisect toggles PERSIST in the pinned palette across runs.** Run #172 opened with `belowWater=False` left from an earlier session, which mimics a fixed bug exactly. Read the bisect line before trusting any water or snow observation.
**⚠ Poll the monitor even when nothing auto-prompts.** Single-occurrence `[RimWorld]` warnings are filtered out of the summaries, and two scatterer-starvation warnings surfaced only that way.
The start-spot failure log is a first-class diagnostic; its cell census identified the coastline bug in one line.

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **Doomed-band genstep scoping pass** (§9). Scope uniformly across non-surface bands; the band-1 heuristic is dead. Record the tile in every measurement.
2. **Verify `0 up / 0 down` reaches generation** (§2). Thirty seconds, and it is both a shipped feature and the lab's only vanilla control.
3. **Audit the other `FalloffAtAngle` mutators**: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley.
4. **Never exercised in play:** multi-hop stair router, elevator, reload fix. **Basement paths are untested**; every run since #172 has been 3-up/0-down, so `surfaceBand=0` and band-folded addressing have never run.
5. Realtime-things pass still single-band (motes and fire more than one level down).
6. Selection bracket drifts upward as you zoom out (that path mixes world and screen space; our offset is in world units).
7. Waterfalls (de-risked by §6b), combat never verified, vertical conduit, compat audit including Better Mountains co-load, **store page still says three levels**.

# 14. LESSONS
**Method.** Prove a subsystem innocent by finding a state where the suspect CANNOT EXIST, rather than instrumenting it. A documented rejection may be re-opened only by naming the confound that invalidated it. Change one thing per experiment. Run the diagnostic before the third theory. An exact number is a diagnosis. Use the product's own knobs as lab equipment. A beautiful fit is not evidence. Not every bug has a bug; knowing when to stop is a result. The absence of a known error line is a valid pass signal.
**⚠ Draw the diagnostic OUTSIDE the thing being diagnosed.** A fallback error message rendered inside a clipped region is silent, and its silence is not evidence. One label outside the scroll view solved in one launch what four launches of theorising could not (§17).
**Claims versus facts.** A comment asserting why something is safe to delete is a claim, not a fact; verify it (§7). Re-measure the assumption you are about to build on (§9). Verify a patched branch is even reachable before debugging your own logic (§16).
**Shapes.** Anything anchored to the map's extent lands in the wrong band; classify it into one of the six shapes. Position-based noise means a slice of a tall map is not a short map. A uniform symptom is a scale or constant, a patchy one is data. An odd/even or count-dependent symptom is arithmetic. When a symptom says "X is missing", ask how many PASSES X takes.
**Patching.** When N call sites share ONE linear mapping, re-aim the shared parameter instead of patching N sites. Find the ONE virtual everything funnels through. Patch the method that PRODUCES a value, not the one that stores it. Patch the idempotent READ, not the cached WRITE. Check whether vanilla reads the cached field or the live property. Own the widget instead of patching the data it reads. Never put a foreign type in a patch-class signature. Read the foreign mod's OWN compat classes first.
**Engine facts.** Defaults matter: `TerrainDef.holdSnowOrSand` defaults TRUE. Altitude is draw order, and `WorldClipper` sorts above `Skyfaller`. A null global texture falls back to the shader's default, not zero. Vanilla divides by a count without guarding zero. A spatial helper that reaches 22 rows will cross a 2-row gutter. `Banded` is FALSE for the whole of map generation, so generation-time patches must read the pending layout. Snapshot generated-world parameters onto the map; never read them live from settings. `SectionLayer` subclasses are auto-discovered by `Section`'s constructor. Any type with a `Material` field needs `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]`. Unity textures are not GC'd with their owner. Statics keyed by game-scoped ids leak; use a CWT. Never cache comps while Scribe is active. FinalizeInit runs on a worker thread. Balance GUI clip and group pops in a `finally`. Ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`. A `Graphic_Linked` base material is the whole atlas sheet. "Can't happen" fallbacks are what the player photographs. Enforce spatial rules per cell.

---

# 15. QOL PASS (verified, run #172)
**15a. Nothing may exist in the void.** `ABBandSafety.cs`. Three redundant layers: the finders (`RandomEdgeCell(Rot4,Map)`, the 5-arg `TryFindRandomEdgeCellWith`, `RandomCell`) answer inside the surface band; a prefix on the 7-arg `GenSpawn.Spawn` (every overload funnels into it) rewrites `loc` before vanilla reads it; a 120-tick sweep using `Position` plus `Notify_Teleported` catches teleports, psycasts, foreign spawners and pre-fix saves. Always relocates to the SURFACE, because a spawn that landed in the void has proven its chooser does not understand bands. Scoped to pawns and to the gutter only; inert during generation, where `RescueStrandedColonists` covers it.
**15b. Structures must not straddle a seam.** `GenGrid.CloseToEdge` measured against `map.Size`, so the surface band reported itself as inland everywhere including the rows that butt onto a seam, silently voiding every generator's edge declaration. One prefix re-bases the distance onto the cell's own band rect and eleven cold call sites inherit it. Backstop: a postfix on `GenStep_Scatterer.CanScatterAt` (the base reaches the whole family, since every stock override opens with `if (!base.CanScatterAt(...)) return false;`). The seam margin is DERIVED (`bandHeight/24`, clamped 4 to 12); a flat 10 starved scatterers on small bands.
**15c. Camera bounds:** `panMargin` 63.5 on every level.
**15d. Vanilla's no-build map edge REMOVED on banded maps.** `ABNoBuildEdge.cs`. Both halves were stack-anchored. Per-band is one flag away (`ABNoBuildEdge.Removed`). Stated consequence: vanilla's strip is also what stops a colony sealing its map edge and starving the pawn-entry finder.
**15e. Drop pods fall through the levels.** `ABSkyfallerRelay.cs`. Two faults, one symptom: the curtain (`WorldClipper`) sorts ABOVE `Skyfaller`, so most of every descent was painted over, and pods bound elsewhere were view-culled. Suppress `Skyfaller.DrawAt` (reached only by skyfallers, unlike `Thing.DynamicDrawPhaseAt` which every dynamic thing walks every frame) and re-issue once via `DrawNowAt`, translated by `(viewedBand - itsBand) * Slot`. Altitude is chosen PER FRAME, or landings render at full brightness through the night lighting overlay. `Skyfaller_FlyingPawn` excluded because it overrides `DrawAt`.

# 16. ALTITUDE AND WEATHER (`ABBandWeather.cs`, verified)
`WeatherManager` is per-Map and there is ONE Map, so weather is not simulated per band. It is one weather INTERPRETED per band.
- **Snow confined to real ground:** `AB_OpenAir` and `AB_WallTop` set `holdSnowOrSand=false`. The default is TRUE, so open air was collecting snow, which on a sky band is the whole screen.
- **Melt per band:** prefix on `DoCellSteadyEffects` rewrites the private `outdoorMeltAmount`, on EVERY call including level 0, or a surface cell inherits whatever the last sky cell installed.
- **Snow must exist before it can persist:** `SeedAltitudeSnow` at generation, depth scaled by how far below freezing, seeded from the CURRENT temperature so a winter start finds the line lower. Only safe because melt is now band-aware.
- **Rain falls and draws as snow above the line.** Accumulation via the public `AddFallenSnowAt`; forcing the private field fails because vanilla gates on the cached field but takes the amount from the live property. Drawing substitutes a snow overlay for the rain one with the colour copied off the rain overlay `SkyManager` just tinted. Rejected: swapping `WeatherDef.Worker.overlays`, which would fix both consumers at once but is a global Def shared across maps.
- **No overlays underground**, judged on the viewed band since overlays are screen-space.
- **Wind x1.15 / x1.30 / x1.50, zero underground.** Patched on the `DesiredPowerOutput` getter, because `CompTick` only recomputes every 250 ticks and a postfix there would compound. Wind-path fix: `CalculateWindCells` spans 22 rows and the gutter is 2, so turbines were blocked by a mountain on a different level.
- **Readout:** `GlobalControls.TemperatureString` rebuilt in a postfix from `TryGetTemperatureForCell`. The first attempt scoped a postfix onto `MapTemperature.OutdoorTemp`, which that method NEVER reaches, because outdoor cells still belong to a Room and `Room.Temperature` is a stored field. `Thing.AmbientTemperature` does route through `GetTemperatureForCell`, so pawns genuinely feel altitude.

# 17. SETTINGS PASS (verified)
**Tabbed and scrolling window:** Performance, Climate, Sky, Basement, Diagnostics. Tab row is hand-drawn buttons, not `TabDrawer` (which paints above the rect it is handed and so depends on space the host `Dialog_ModSettings` owns). Each tab draws inside a try/catch that renders the exception into the pane, because a settings panel that shows its own failure beats one that silently draws nothing.

**⚠ The blank-tab bug, and the lesson that cost four launches.** Scroll-view content height is measured from the previous frame's `list.CurHeight`, because a `Listing_Standard` only knows its height after drawing. Without a floor this is a SELF-SUSTAINING LATCH: any frame that draws short stores a tiny height, the next frame hands the scroll view that tiny rect which clips everything past it, so the frame after measures short again. Climate latched at `viewH=40`, showing only its heading, and the clipped region included the try/catch's own error text, so the silence looked like proof the method never ran. Performance escaped only because its content fit inside the initial 600px seed on its first frame, which made one working tab out of five look exactly like a tab-dispatch failure. Fix: `viewHeights[i] = Mathf.Max(list.CurHeight + 16f, inner.height)`. Diagnosed by one label drawn OUTSIDE the scroll view reporting tab and rect values.

**The unlock gate.** The checkbox writes to a LOCAL; `unclampMapSize` only becomes true inside the confirmation callback, so the stored value IS the record that the warning was read, and no separate acknowledgement flag can drift out of sync. Turning it back off is never gated. While unlocked, a red banner on the tab and the colony-creation strip reports the multiple over budget. That strip colours against the BUDGET, not against `Fits()`, because once unlocked `Fits()` is unconditionally true, which is exactly when the warning matters most.
**The budget stays a `const`**, deliberately. A slider invites nudging and every nudge walks someone further into unsupported territory without the dialog ever firing.
**Climate is SNAPSHOTTED onto `ABBandMap` at generation** (`SnapshotClimate`, scribed, called beside `Setup` on BOTH carve paths). Resolution order is snapshot, then settings, then hardcoded defaults, so pre-snapshot saves and mid-generation calls still answer. Reading live settings would re-climate every existing save.
Always shows 3 up and 3 down regardless of the current plan, so a layout can be tuned before it is chosen. Presets Gentle, Standard, Alpine. Each slider previews the resulting temperature against the live map, or 20 degrees from the menu.

## TESTING RULE
`isolated=true`, `quicktest=false` (the level chooser needs the menus; Map Preview doubly so, since the preview only exists on the world map).
Compat tests need the target mod as a companion. Dubs (`dubwise.dubsmintminimap`) and Map Preview (`m00nl1ght.MapPreview`) are both INACTIVE in the user's real list.
Water tests need a river or lake tile, coastline tests a coastal one, and a tile with NO water mutators is sometimes the most valuable of all (§6b-LAKE). Note the tile in any perf comparison.
A `surfaceBand=0` config cannot exercise band-folded addressing.
Read the bisect line before trusting any water or snow observation.
